rules: Do not convert witness travel estimates into exact arrival times.
Shared vehicle crews receive one arrival event until their actions diverge.
The scream/child alert is the central synchronization event prompting discovery/response to the children.
Josephine's ambulance-backing statement constrains Dawson's extraction after the scream; it does not place Dawson before the scream.
Occurrence time and proceeding/testimony time remain distinct.
T₀ is the scream/child alert. It is a synchronization node, not a clock time: each witness is aligned by what they were doing immediately before and after it.
An assertion is placed before, at, or after T₀ only when the witness ties it to the scream or to an event that is itself tied to it. Everything else stays unplaced.
Sources cite the witness's transcript position, not the time of the event.
Where two witnesses use the same first name, the record keeps them apart: in Stratton's testimony “Patrick” is firefighter Patrick Dwyer.

anchor.label: Scream / child alert
anchor.definition: The loud scream (Stratton: a voice yelling that a child was in the basement) that most responders describe just before they went, or were sent, into the house to the children.
anchor.rationale: The witnesses do not need to agree on a clock time. Each independently describes their own position immediately before and after the same occurrence, so their accounts can be sequenced against each other without inventing timestamps.

before.text: Outside. Sees Patrick standing over Lindsay with a phone at his side; Patrick passes him toward the deck without speaking. Talks with Lindsay 30–60 seconds until fire personnel arrive and take over.

at.text: Standing by the window with Hall; hears loud screams. Unsure whether dispatch said anything about the basement.

after.text: Deck, slider, kitchen, basement; follows the screaming to the right. Patrick comes out of the back room. Finds Dawson, carries him up and out the front door to Ambulance 1, then returns and works on Cora.

before.text: Outside. Directs arriving fire to the side gate. Patrick says he is going inside to check on his children. Radio: dispatch says Patrick “couldn't wake them up.”

at.text: Hears a loud scream from inside the house, “just a sound.”

after.text: Runs with Josephine to the slider and kitchen; says the screaming had stopped. Basement, right; Patrick: “I can't wake them up.” Finds Dawson, calls for paramedics, goes back down and left to the other two children, later returns outside to Lindsay.

before.text: Outside, left of the window well, supervising while paramedics treat Lindsay.

at.text: Hears a scream that seems to come from the basement.

after.text: Looks through the basement window well and sees Patrick lifting a child and unwrapping something from around the head and neck. Puts in an all-call recall and requests a mutual-aid ambulance; later requests two more.

before.text: Treating Lindsay: places an oral airway, then a non-rebreather oxygen mask.

at.text: “From there, that's when we heard the scream.” He, Hussey and Heath look at each other.

after.text: Hussey leaves; Heath goes for a backboard and does not return with it. Dougherty stays with Lindsay and bandages her wrists (bandaging came after the scream). Hall later brings the board.

witness_alignment.role: Duxbury firefighter-paramedic (no testimony of his own; per Dougherty and Nette)

after.text: Leaves Lindsay to get a backboard. Nette later finds Heath in Ambulance 1 doing CPR on Dawson with Sergeant Homestead. Heath's own path in between is not stated.

before.text: Arrives to a cruiser in the driveway, an ambulance and a fire captain; goes to the backyard where Lindsay is already being cared for.

after.text: Goes inside and down the stairs. Sees Patrick crossing from Cahill's left to right, screaming; Patrick points left. Finds Cora and Callan, checks pulses, steps back when fire arrives, later moves the futon, fetches equipment and gives rescue breaths on Cora.

before.text: Engine 2 arrives just after Ambulance 1. In the backyard, sees Dougherty kneeling by a person in the dark; “that was all we saw for a few seconds.”

at.text: Hears a voice yelling for them to get inside, that there is a kid hanging in the basement. She does not describe a scream.

after.text: Slider, kitchen, basement, left. Sees Callan and Cora face up. Radios for two additional ambulances and goes to Callan; Dwyer goes to Cora.

before.text: Arrives with Stratton in the dark; other firefighters are already there. Walking toward the backyard on the left side.

at.text: Redirected to the basement while walking toward the backyard.

after.text: Through the backyard and slider, down and left: two children on the ground and “the father sitting on the couch next to them.” Starts CPR on Cora.

patrick_positions.intro: Every position responders place Patrick Clancy in, relative to T₀. Each is one witness's observation from one vantage point.

entries.text: Standing over Lindsay with a phone at his side, then passes Josephine near the bulkhead toward the deck without speaking.
Says he is going inside to check on his children and heads for the back slider. Shortly after, the radio says he “couldn't wake them up.”
Seen through the basement window lifting a child and unwrapping something from around the head and neck.
In the back room on the right; comes toward the officers and says “She killed the fucking kids.”
Talking from the basement, then comes from the back room saying “I can't wake them up. I can't get them up.”
On the stairs, sees Patrick moving from Cahill's left to right, screaming; Patrick points left toward Cora and Callan.
Seated on a couch next to the two children on the floor of the left room when Engine 2 arrives.
Later, in the kitchen: frantic, in shock, still screaming; an ambulance is requested for him.
At the hospital emergency department, visibly upset, after the children had been pronounced.

not_attested: No responder transcript in this set describes Patrick performing CPR on any child. His own accounts of what he did are not in this folder yet, so this is the responders' side only.
Only Dwyer describes Patrick seated next to the children in the left room. Only Hussey describes him unwrapping something from a child. Each is a single witness.

No responder transcript reports Patrick telling them, before he went inside, that the children were in the basement or were hurt. Josephine says he passed without speaking; Hall says he said he was going to check on his children; dispatch relayed the basement and 'couldn't wake them up' from the open 911 line. Lindsay had told him the children were in the basement (his trial testimony).

lanes.label: Lindsay care
lanes.summary: Care for Lindsay in the backyard runs on both sides of T₀ and gives the strongest before/after chain.

lanes.label: Dawson
lanes.summary: From the scream to Ambulance 1. Josephine's “ambulance was backing up and had pretty much just parked” ties his exit to Nudd's stretcher.

lanes.label: Cora and Callan
lanes.summary: Cahill reaches the left room first; Engine 2 follows; Hall and Josephine return after Dawson is out.

discrepancies.issue: Did the screaming continue in the kitchen?
assertions: Josephine: in the kitchen it was “the exact screaming that I heard from the window” (37:35).
Hall: in the kitchen “the screaming was done” and Patrick could be heard talking (12:57).
discrepancies.handling: Both preserved on FR052. The witnesses entered together.

discrepancies.issue: What was the alert: a scream or a voice?
assertions: Josephine, Hall, Hussey, Dougherty, Cahill: a scream.
Stratton: a voice yelling for them to get inside because “a kid [was] hanging in the basement” (01:38:12).
Dwyer: says only that they were directed to the basement (01:24:31).
discrepancies.handling: Kept on one anchor node because each account prompts the same response. The speaker of Stratton's words is not identified.

discrepancies.issue: Where was Patrick Clancy in the basement, and when?
assertions: Hussey, Josephine, Hall: in or coming from the right back room where Dawson lay.
Cahill: crossing from his left to right on the stairs, then pointing left.
Dwyer: seated on a couch beside Cora and Callan in the left room.
discrepancies.handling: Recorded as separate observations. Their order relative to each other is not established by the transcripts.

assertions: Stratton: “Patrick ran to Cora and I went to Callan” (01:38:50). This is firefighter Patrick Dwyer, not Patrick Clancy.
discrepancies.handling: Noted in the method rules so the two are never merged.

discrepancies.issue: Who fetched the backboard for Lindsay?
assertions: Dougherty: Heath left for the board and did not return with it; Hall came to the backyard, was told where it was, brought it, and helped load her (02:01:59–02:02:55).
Hall: describes returning outside because an officer was needed with Lindsay and replacing her oxygen mask; he does not mention fetching the board (22:59–26:26).
discrepancies.handling: Not necessarily a contradiction. FR034 stays attributed to Dougherty; Hall's account is on FR060.

discrepancies.issue: The window well: what Josephine and Hall were standing near
assertions: Josephine: he and Hall were standing by the window when they heard the screams (36:54).
Hall: he had gone to the gate to direct fire personnel and Patrick had gone inside before the scream (11:20–12:24).
discrepancies.handling: Compatible if the officers were near the window and the gate at different moments. Left unplaced.
